lines: An Ambient Church Organ Piece I Heard
A cascade of notes— held.
Each one a moon reflecting in the spectral ripples of the lake
Beneath the red mountains.
The buzz of shifting tectonic plates in my ribcage,
Subduction pressing my shoulders down,
down into the earth—
The note changes.
Cabin in the snow
Cabin swallowed beneath the bright world of snow crackling heavy breathing
Singing clinging embracing
Through a mirror clouding a sight buried in bright grass under feet of powder
Birch songs
groaning brushing painting a shag carpet to rub our feet into
How the ice holds up the snow and the water up the ice
In a block somewhere we can all meet
You'll knock and the wind will howl the door open to stillness
Never to return

What lives behind darkness but the effervescent desire? For the light in our flag misses the corners and in those interstices things grow, bleached and sickening. Whispering. Chanting. The only cave that can truly be lit up is assembled from red mud and sticks, and what kind of matinee is that?

This is special. Lights on tree with frogs and stars behind illuminating a quilt draped over the skeleton of a tree, drying. Movement behind observer and grass giving grants. Pinholes to wishupon and dragons to be afraid of. Ghosts down the middle of suburban streets observed by one. We fly because we take ourselves lightly.
Carousel of trees
Pine needles beneath snow to the hissing pressure of what sleeps below
Berries and sticks and actual magic
Midnight cathedrals and caricatures of castles
Sparks of stone silhouette behind walls
Mountains move to the old dogs calls
Forgotten gods a statues darling
A raft for two
A thriving garden
Smoking trees move in groups shifting carousels converge at the point the light stops
Cosmic comedy
In your house the walls do sing
Stories about your tattooed ring
Yet still we forget and yearn to be
The graveyard opens and lets us see
Thrashing others but granting sight
A son guided by its mother through the night
but when spotted, that golden chain wakes up and realizes its all the same
Giant corpse in the sky beating down in a rainbows eye
Seeded growth in a maze mind
Shoots towards shared light
Creator of eidolons
What shelters do I build and what do I gain from showing them off?
The presence of a camera haunts this field, a ghost in a poem of apparitions, A shelter criticized yet cradling.
Leaves of grass have said
"Lo, I or you,
Or woman, man, or state, known or unknown,
We seeming solid wealth, strength, beauty build,
But really build eidolons."
Eidolons fill this cave, singing a song of all divinity. flipping a single sided coin of heads and tails. watching mountains of sun and shadow. I see what I see and say what's already been said.
Here ill stay, in from the rain, fashioning eidolons
Feel this page and know it
Kiln street - Ode to Lynch
This fire coursing through my veins
entered uninvited but welcome to stay
reflected on the sky, something was lost
walk with me blind, hands made of frost
The flames in the wind but the rivers within
flowing beneath these hollow streets
the fire still burns, unbothered and free
Followed to a gate, a sycamore tree
there is no lock and there is no key
this wooden world
one longs to see
a blaze burning bright
fire walk with me
Man made of stone
once crafted from flame
now walks alone
forgotten his name
Flower tiles yearn
to play a game
masters of nothing
cured in the blaze
Living torch
All is silent and black
The moon blinks and becomes full from nothing
The hill screams and erupts
The pencil sketched ground is illuminated by the hand of god
Biology textbooks hit the ground and split open
The hill erupts once more and from its peak a river of lava descends upon Primordia
(Ferns sway out of its path)
The hill gurgles and from the pool of molten rock a stone human rises
Unmoving, it descends on its raft
My vision sways and I join the statue
An offering for the first man
The palm trees bend down and lift me up with their fronds
Lava turns over granite hills and tills the soil beneath
The torrent of flame joins all things
Suddenly all is known and the palm trees lift me higher above the clouds
The footsteps of an empty olympus
Hearth flameless, coals still smoking becoming clouds, becoming rain, dousing the cataclysm below
Gazing down, the lava river has hardened and little yellow stripes line its middle
The hills have melted, leaving behind bricks
Meadow
Bunny digs for stars in the meadow
Covers of twilight, violins, and cellos
Songs of children whisper and bellow
Yet here, floods with water
Gardens spring from a sandy patch
Tools stored where memories shed
Entertainment for a man that laughs
Fall asleep leaves a bed
I wish I knew just a little bit more
Suburbs I
At midnight, a McMansion stands.
Below, pot lights erase its shadows,
its face flattened into a veneer.
The sprinklers maintain the lawn—
a seamless quadrilateral,
its mist crawling over the stretch of empty road,
where a single pylon sits deliberately in its center–
no damage nearby.
Suburbs II
A pedestrian light counts down for nobody.
Beside it, a closed café
glows from the inside
where a radio hums a muffled song.
Further down, a fuel station.
Its tankers sit empty.
A single rabbit sits in its light.
The road opens to the forest
where the insects hum the whole night through.
Summer night porch
The summer night porch swings its fist through the wind tunnel into my throat
I caught its wooden hands and they struck twice, telling me it was time to leave
Canes made from cane made from dirt made from aspartame
My hands bled in solitude though filled my cup with blackberries
The throne of gold I sat on makes my Dirty Silver Dance seem so 6 months ago
Even as I write this I see ants crawling up my leg and the pendulum drawing back for another jab
Sit down and stare
Taking a picture where frogs frown and worms indeed drown
I took a picture where frogs frown and worms indeed drown
A ball of crystal falls from its socket
Caught by a man with masks in his pocket
He wrote a poem about a dream he had
Streets made of fire rejecting desire
Man and stone by one speaking in tongue
Cuckoo clock eyes revealing disguise
The Archive
When you had to leave,
the guiltiest part of me wishes I could fossilize your dear plant.
That I could encase it in amber resin.
Or gently flatten it into some academic's leather-bound tome underneath the warmth of a desk lamp—
only to file it away into one of a thousand metal drawers.
Resin stains the fingertips like rust.
That damn dirty, charcoal-gum amber.
Even then, a root might still crack through the drawer.
I could never do it.
But I love you.
The Bear In The Forest
The black.
Under a dead sky.
Formless then
The single blade of light sweeps fast across the forest
illuminates each slice of the stillness
illuminates for an instant
the slick and sheen
of its matted fur
caked in mud.
Again,
the blade of light sweeps the stillness fast,
but
some shadow has shifted
less than sight can catch
but enough to feel.
Again
the blade of light sweeps faster
faster faster
dim shine in its
obsidian irises
faster
its hunched figure backlit
closer
a frame
closer
a frame a frame a Frame
Its
Eyes
my body jolts awake
in the cold sweat of my sheets
the fourth
time
that
night
it waits in the blade
The unobserved woods and the crested meadow
The unobserved woods like the uncreated moment exists only in my mind
I set up a tent and watched the sunset knowing exactly what I'd find
Though the tree branches sway in a way they all stay the same
I knew the way out would not be the in way I came
The lying moon sold me to mars and mars to the stars
And with the money he made he built a ladder so tall
So tall above us all
Rooms we never knew existed behind our walls
Crumbs in cracks incomprehensible
The real dawn and the one I hold in my palm
To grasp a mountain you'd need a pretty big hand
Giant mugs are often filled with nothing
Thick white mist
oh thick white mist you hide the buildings in my life
what is fulfulling and what is my strife
what are my songs and how should I play them
where are my friends, and where did you lay them
where are my seeds, and how should I sow them
where are my leaves, and how do i grow them?
you songs are finished and you already know them
your friends are here
your seeds are tall cause you already grow them
your fulfilling doesnt matter
your strife is living so do not hurt him
within me they grow
through layers of snow
in spring they will fruit
through stem and root
give them some time
and your mist will clear
the buildings stand tall
you are no longer small
there are no more questions
there are no more lies
we do nothing I see nothing
rotting filled with maggots
I convinced myself to live forever and then come back again
I made the knife that killed his wife dividing son and sin
And on our roof a thin lid lies for medals made of tin
These things all end up within
Whimsy
I burnt my waffles today.
They looked like manhole covers.
So look at the world!
I've been walking on waffles this whole time.
